record.body:
## Rationale

`dashboard/phase_screen.py`, `dashboard/task_detail.py`, `dashboard/requirement_detail.py`, and `dashboard/journal.py` are already the screen seams. The model splits the same way: snapshot, task, phase, and requirement modules, with store access in its own module. `dashboard/model.py` cannot sit beside a `dashboard/model/` package, so the file becomes that package and `dashboard/model/__init__.py` re-exports the names callers already import. Screen classes other than `DashboardApp` leave `dashboard/app.py`. The model package does not import Textual or Rich, which is how `tests/test_dashboard_model.py` and the web reader use it today.

## Counter-argument

A vertical slice would put each screen in the same module as the rows it draws, so a phase-view change would be one file. The model package plus the existing screen modules splits that feature in two. Colocating them would make the data modules import Textual, and the model tests and the web service would take on the UI library.

payload.alternatives: Layer split of queries, row types, and screens; vertical slices that put Textual screens in the same module as row types
payload.choice: Split dashboard.model along snapshot, task, phase, and requirement, move the remaining screens out of app.py, and keep dashboard.model as a facade
